turn.subject: solution
turn.user_message: Show me the people who must agree

text: Several teams touch discharge, but only a few are asked to change much. One person has to approve it. Why each matters:
bullets: Doctors are asked for no extra time. They already decide at 7 PM, which is why they can agree.
Typists have the most to give up, so they check drafts first, and nobody loses a job at the start.
The Head of Operations must approve the new order, or it won’t last past the first busy morning.
chat.invite: Next is who is in charge: whether you need anyone new. Shall we go there?
chat.note: Help first. Fewer hands only once it is trusted.

points.label: Typists, who have the most to give up

prompts: Show me who is in charge
Our consultants won’t sign on a phone

blocks.eyebrow: Part 3 of 5 · People who must agree
blocks.title: Who has to say yes

doers.ask: Say who is going home at 7 PM, then sign on a phone next morning.
Check and correct a ready draft, instead of typing each one from scratch.
Check what the software writes down, instead of counting supplies before billing.
Check bills that are already made, instead of building them after signing.
Link the software to patient records, bills, lab reports and scans.
Act when the software says a bed or a patient is ready.

approver.approves: The new order of steps, and splitting discharges from admissions.
approver.fails_if: the first busy morning sends everyone back to the old order.

blocks.caption: Each team is told the software takes work off them first. Fewer staff comes later, and only once it is trusted.
